source: gearbook repo, docs/marketing/social-identity.md and content-idea-bank.md (drafts of 2026-10-16, seeded from the live feed, Luke corrects them)

audiences.name: Outdoor professionals
audiences.who: Instructors, athletes, mountain guides and others who work outdoors, across every sport GearBook's partners cover.

audiences.name: Their clients and followers
audiences.who: People who buy through a member's page. Posts aimed only at them have done worst so far, so use them sparingly.

sportsNote: All of them, rotated across posts. Scuba.com and West Marine are partners, so don't let the account become mountain-only.

onCamera.role: The default talent, in the presenter bit. Presented as GearBook's founder who uses the gear, never as a certified guide.
Trip montages and vibe reels, tagged in captions.
An upgrade whenever one opts in, never relied on. Rare in October 2026.

onCameraRule: Anyone on camera gives their OK. Footage and photos are credited to whoever shot them.

formats.name: Presenter bit
formats.what: Luke in a suit, tie and handheld mic plays a deadpan presenter somewhere absurd for a suit: a desk on a cliff, rappelling, sitting in a creek, buried in ropes. Short script to camera, about 25 to 30 s.
formats.edit: Captions burned in, meme overlays (a coin pile, a crying-emoji map), product cutouts flying in, a screen recording for a partner's catalog, ending on the logo or the brand colour bars.

formats.name: Vibe reel
formats.what: No voice. Good footage, one line of meme text, a trending sound added in the app.
formats.edit: Quick to make from footage you and friends already have.

formats.name: Editorial poster
formats.what: A still: a duotone or moody photo with text in the brand serif.

bit.script: What if every time you recommended your favorite gear, you got paid? I'm Luke, and this is GearBook.
bit.joke: A straight-faced corporate presenter in places no suit belongs. The outdoor setting is real, and the gear and the information are real too.

voice: Dry humour, meme overlays, emojis (🤙), "get stoked", "make some cash"
Short captions: one or two lines, then "Click the link in our bio"
rules: Never promise an amount or quote a rate. Talking about getting paid is fine; numbers live on /commission-rates.
No em or en dashes, in any copy.
No urgency theatre or fake deals.
Safety topics (avalanche, diving depth) are played straight: no jokes, no instruction.
taste: Ideas he can post, built around one person's real kit tied to a job, a season or a moment.
Keep it positive: what people carry and love, not what they dropped or dislike.
Skip pro-deal and discount angles (Outdoor Prolink, ExpertVoice). They're where pros buy, not where they earn.
Content is made in the week of posting. Ideas keep loose windows, not dates.
worst: The generic shopper pitch and the generic seasonal tip did worst (24 and 27 likes). Lead with the bit or the footage, and put the pitch last.

maybeLater.name: Black Friday no-sale report
maybeLater.what: The presenter bit with "Today's top deal: going outside." No real deals. Don't use REI's #OptOutside tag.

maybeLater.name: Giving Tuesday
maybeLater.what: Groups that keep trails, forecasts and access running. Don't imply GearBook donates unless that's decided.

maybeLater.name: Home-shopping-channel gift list
maybeLater.what: A shopping-host parody, but with real picks and why, and no fake urgency.

maybeLater.name: Avalanche season
maybeLater.what: Played straight, no jokes. "Take a course, read your local forecast." No kit claims without avalanche training.

maybeLater.name: Course notes
maybeLater.what: The kit that held up. No technique or rescue advice.

maybeLater.name: Get to know a pro
maybeLater.what: A short profile with 3 to 5 picks.

toFill: Who's on the team (Matt's role in content, the photographer, the editor), and which friends or members are happy to be on camera.
Where the presenter bit came from, what it should never become, and whether it stays Luke-only.
Instagram Insights per post (reach, saves, shares, non-follower reach, average watch time). Likes alone may mislead.
Where raw footage lives, and roughly what's there by sport and person.
A swipe file: about 5 posts from any account you'd love to have made, and 3 you'd never post, each with a few words on why.
